interviewBank.q: What is the difference between content-box and border-box?
interviewBank.answer: content-box adds padding and border outside the declared width. border-box includes them inside it, so width means the visible box. Most projects set border-box globally.
Adjacent block margins in normal flow combine into the larger of the two instead of adding, and a parent and first child can collapse too. Padding, borders, flex or grid contexts stop it.

defenseBank.q: A learner sets width 100% and gets a scrollbar.
defenseBank.answer: The padding and border are being added outside the width. border-box makes the declared width include them, which is why it is the usual global reset.

defenseBank.q: Why not use margins for inner spacing?
defenseBank.answer: Margin is outside the border and can collapse with neighbours; padding is inside and belongs to the element’s own surface.
steps: Show a background that stops at the padding.

mcqBank.q: Which value includes padding and border in the declared width?
mcqBank.why: border-box makes width the visible box.

mcqBank.q: Which side is outside the border?
mcqBank.why: Margin is the outermost spacing layer.

interviewBank.q: display:none or visibility:hidden — which do you use?
interviewBank.answer: display:none removes the element from layout, accessibility and tab order. visibility:hidden keeps the space but hides the element. Choose by whether the space should exist.

interviewBank.q: What does inline-block give you that inline does not?
interviewBank.answer: It stays in the text flow like an inline box but accepts width, height and vertical margins, which makes it useful for chips and older nav patterns.

defenseBank.q: A learner tries to center a span with width.
defenseBank.answer: An inline box ignores width. Make it inline-block or put the centring on the block parent instead.

defenseBank.q: Why prefer flex over inline-block for navigation?
defenseBank.answer: Flex handles gaps, alignment and wrapping without whitespace artefacts between inline-blocks, and it keeps working when labels change length.

mcqBank.q: What is the default display of a div?
mcqBank.why: A div is a block-level element by default.

mcqBank.q: Which value removes an element from layout entirely?
mcqBank.why: Only display:none removes the box from layout.

topics.body: Outline layout me jagah nahi leta aur radius follow nahi karta. Focus indicators ke liye yahi use hota hai, border ki jagah nahi.

<!DOCTYPE html>

    button { border: 1px solid #cbd5e1; padding: 10px 16px; border-radius: 8px; }
    button:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #2563eb; outline-offset: 2px; }
  </style>
</head>
<body>
  <button type="button">Focus me</button>
</body>
</html>
topics.output: A bordered button that gets a 3px blue outline 2px outside its edge when focused by keyboard.

interviewBank.answer: Outline, because it does not affect layout, can be offset from the edge, and is designed for focus indication. Removing it without a replacement breaks keyboard accessibility.
A tight, darker shadow suggests contact while a wide, lighter one suggests ambient light. Together they read as real depth without looking like a blurry halo.

defenseBank.q: A designer asks for a 1px border that does not change size.
defenseBank.answer: A border adds to the box unless border-box is set. With border-box the border is drawn inside the declared width and the layout stays put.

defenseBank.q: Why not use box-shadow instead of a border?
defenseBank.answer: A shadow is paint only; it does not define the element’s edge, does not print reliably and cannot replace the visual boundary for high-contrast users.

mcqBank.q: Which shadow draws inside the element?

interviewBank.q: What containing block does an absolute element use?
interviewBank.answer: The nearest ancestor with a position other than static, or a transform, filter or container-type that establishes one. Without such an ancestor it uses the initial containing block.

interviewBank.q: How is sticky different from fixed?
interviewBank.answer: Sticky stays in normal flow until the scroll reaches its inset threshold, then behaves as if fixed within its containing block. Fixed is always relative to the viewport.

defenseBank.q: A learner uses absolute for the whole page layout.
defenseBank.answer: Absolute removes elements from flow, so nothing reserves their space and overlapping is inevitable. Flow, flex or grid should own layout; absolute is for overlays and badges.

defenseBank.q: Why does a huge z-index still sit behind?
defenseBank.answer: Stacking contexts compare siblings inside one context, not numbers across contexts. A parent with a lower context wins over every child inside it.
steps: Move the element to the right context.

mcqBank.q: Which position value is the default?
mcqBank.why: Static is the initial position value.

interviewBank.q: Flexbox or Grid — how do you choose?
interviewBank.answer: Flexbox distributes items along one axis and is content-driven. Grid defines rows and columns together and is layout-driven. Use flex for a bar or a row of chips, grid for a page or gallery.

interviewBank.q: Why does a flex item refuse to shrink?
interviewBank.answer: A flex item’s automatic minimum size is its content size, so long unbreakable content can prevent shrinking. min-width:0 (or overflow handling) lets it shrink below that.

defenseBank.answer: auto margins work in flex but are less explicit than justify-content and fail in wrapping or multi-line cases. Alignment properties express the intent.
steps: Add a second line and compare.

defenseBank.q: Why set gap instead of margins between items?
defenseBank.answer: Gap belongs to the container, so it does not add space at the outer edges and does not collapse. Margins have to be undone on the first or last child.

mcqBank.q: Which property aligns items on the cross axis?
mcqBank.why: align-items works across the cross axis.
It is the common shorthand for equal flexible items.

interviewBank.q: What is the difference between auto-fit and auto-fill?
interviewBank.answer: auto-fill keeps empty tracks and leaves blank space; auto-fit collapses empty tracks so the existing items stretch to fill the row. Galleries usually want auto-fit.
Tracks the browser creates automatically when items are placed outside the explicit template. It is why an extra item still lands somewhere sensible.

defenseBank.q: A learner uses flex for a two-dimensional page.
defenseBank.answer: Flex aligns along one axis; a page with a header, sidebar and main area is two-dimensional. Grid expresses the rows and columns directly.
steps: Draw the layout as a grid.

defenseBank.q: Why use minmax in a gallery?
defenseBank.answer: It sets a floor so tiles never get too narrow and a ceiling of 1fr so they share the remaining space, which removes the need for breakpoints.

mcqBank.q: Which unit distributes free space in a grid?
mcqBank.why: The fr unit represents a fraction of the free space.

mcqBank.q: Which property names a grid area?

interviewBank.answer: The base styles target the smallest, most constrained layout, and min-width queries add capability. It keeps the default CSS simple and avoids undoing desktop rules on small screens.

interviewBank.q: When is a container query better than a media query?
interviewBank.answer: When a component’s layout depends on its own available width rather than the viewport — a card in a sidebar and the same card in a wide main column should adapt independently.

defenseBank.q: A learner picks breakpoints from device names.
defenseBank.answer: Devices change every year and the layout only cares about its own width. I resize until the content breaks, then put the query there.
steps: Add the query at that width.

defenseBank.answer: An image with intrinsic width larger than its container overflows and causes horizontal scrolling. max-width plus height auto keeps it fluid and proportional.

mcqBank.q: Which query targets screens at least 640px wide?

mcqBank.q: Which meta tag is required for mobile layout?

title: Pseudo-Classes

topics.title: Interaction states
topics.body: hover, active aur focus-visible user interaction ke states hain. focus-visible keyboard focus par lagta hai, isliye mouse click par unnecessary ring nahi aata.
topics.code:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8">
  <title>States</title>
  <style>
    .btn { background: #2563eb; color: #fff; padding: 10px 16px; border: 0; border-radius: 8px; }
    .btn:hover { background: #1d4ed8; }
    .btn:active { transform: translateY(1px); }
    .btn:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #93c5fd; outline-offset: 2px; }
  </style>
</head>
<body>
  <button class="btn" type="button">Save</button>
</body>
</html>
topics.output: Blue button that darkens on hover, moves down 1px when pressed, and shows a light blue focus ring from the keyboard.

interviewBank.answer: :focus matches every focus, including a mouse click. :focus-visible matches when the browser judges that focus should be visible, which is usually keyboard navigation. Use it for rings.

interviewBank.q: Why does :where exist when :is can do the same grouping?
interviewBank.answer: :where always contributes zero specificity, which makes it ideal for resets and base styles that must not outrank component rules.

defenseBank.q: A designer wants the focus ring removed.
defenseBank.answer: The ring is the only signal a keyboard user has. We can restyle it to match the brand, but not remove it.
When a parent must react to a child’s state and no class is being set by script, such as marking a field wrapper invalid. Where script already sets a class, that class is simpler.
